stem: Which nursing practice set is part of CDC Standard Precautions for routine patient care?

options.A: Hand hygiene, exposure-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, safe injection and sharps practices, and appropriate cleaning of equipment and the environment.
options.B: A fit-tested respirator and an airborne-infection isolation room for every patient regardless of diagnosis or exposure risk.
options.C: A gown and gloves for every room entry regardless of anticipated contact with blood, body fluids, mucous membranes, or contaminated material.
options.D: Precautions only after a transmissible infection is laboratory-confirmed, with no routine infection-prevention measures before confirmation.

rationale: CDC states that Standard Precautions are used for all patient care and are based on risk assessment. They include hand hygiene; PPE when infectious-material exposure is anticipated; respiratory hygiene/cough etiquette; safe injection and sharps practices; and appropriate handling, cleaning, and disinfection of patient-care equipment and the environment. Therefore A is correct. B describes airborne-specific controls applied universally, not Standard Precautions. C ignores the risk-based nature of PPE use. D is incorrect because Standard Precautions apply to all patient care rather than only after laboratory confirmation.
educational_objective: Identify the core CDC Standard Precautions used for all patient care, including hand hygiene, risk-based PPE, respiratory hygiene, injection/sharps safety, and environmental/equipment cleaning.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)

correction_summary: Retained the Standard Precautions construct but rebuilt the alternatives to test the risk-based boundary between Standard Precautions and transmission-based practices. Moved the correct answer from B to A, removed the weak 'hand hygiene alone' distractor, and anchored the blueprint to the exact NCSBN 2026 Safety and Infection Prevention and Control activity statement on printed page 8/PDF page 12.

audit_findings.option_D: Wrong — Standard Precautions are used for all patient care and do not wait for laboratory confirmation.
